edges.description: Claudin-16 is a cation (Na+) pore in TAL tight junctions; with claudin-19 it makes the junction cation selective. Disease variants abolish this.
edges.target: Loss of Cation-Selective TAL Tight Junction Pathway

edges.description: Claudin-16 is also expressed at secretory ameloblast tight junctions, where its loss alters enamel formation.
Without a cation-selective paracellular pathway, magnesium and calcium are no longer reabsorbed in the TAL.
edges.source: Loss of Cation-Selective TAL Tight Junction Pathway
edges.target: Impaired Paracellular Magnesium and Calcium Reabsorption in the TAL

edges.description: Proposed: claudin-16 may also be needed for tight junction integrity, and its loss may drive progressive kidney injury independently of the calcium load. Supported only by the genotype-dependence of kidney decline, not by a direct experiment.

edges.description: Parathyroid hormone rises before kidney failure, in contrast to the low or normal PTH usually seen with hypomagnesemia. In the knockout mouse the rise is interpreted as compensation for renal calcium loss.
edges.source: Impaired Paracellular Magnesium and Calcium Reabsorption in the TAL

edges.description: Urinary calcium loss leads to calcium deposition in the kidney. Mice with Cldn16 knockdown develop nephrocalcinosis but mice with targeted Cldn16 deletion do not, so compensation can modify this step.
Knockdown mice lose TAL paracellular cation selectivity and develop renal magnesium and calcium wasting with nephrocalcinosis.
edges.limitations: Knockdown is incomplete and transgenic, unlike germline biallelic human variants; progressive kidney failure is not reported in this model.
edges.target: Loss of Cation-Selective TAL Tight Junction Pathway

edges.description: Knockout mice have hypercalciuria and hypomagnesemia with raised PTH and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, but no nephrocalcinosis.
edges.limitations: Compensatory upregulation of calcium and magnesium transporters prevents nephrocalcinosis, so the model does not reproduce the human calcium deposition or kidney failure.
edges.target: Impaired Paracellular Magnesium and Calcium Reabsorption in the TAL

nodes.description: Claudin-16 localizes to tight junctions of secretory ameloblasts. Its loss alters their structure, acidifies the forming enamel matrix and disturbs enamel matrix protein processing.

evidence.reference_title: Claudin-16 Deficiency Impairs Tight Junction Function in Ameloblasts, Leading to Abnormal Enamel Formation.
evidence.snippet: To investigate the role of CLDN16 in tooth formation, we studied a murine model of FHHNC and showed that CLDN16 deficiency led to altered secretory ameloblast TJ structure, lowering of extracellular pH in the forming enamel matrix, and abnormal enamel matrix protein processing, resulting in an enamel phenotype closely resembling human AI.

evidence.reference_title: Claudin-16 Deficiency Impairs Tight Junction Function in Ameloblasts, Leading to Abnormal Enamel Formation.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate the expression of CLDN16 also in the tooth germ and show that claudin-16 gene (CLDN16) mutations result in amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) in the 5 studied patients with familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis (FHHNC).

nodes.description: Missense, nonsense, splice-site and deletion variants in CLDN16 reduce or abolish claudin-16 function. Expression studies separate variants that leave partial function from those that abolish it, and the distinction predicts age at onset and rate of kidney decline. Missense variants cluster in the first extracellular loop; p.Leu151Phe is a founder allele in Germany and eastern Europe.

evidence.reference_title: Paracellin-1, a renal tight junction protein required for paracellular Mg2+ resorption.
evidence.snippet: Here, positional cloning has identified a human gene, paracellin-1 (PCLN-1), mutations in which cause renal Mg2+ wasting.

evidence.reference_title: CLDN16 genotype predicts renal decline in familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.
evidence.snippet: Expression studies revealed that five of the 12 new mutations led to partial loss of claudin-16 function and the remaining seven led to complete loss of function.

evidence.reference_title: CLDN16 / renal hypomagnesemia 3 (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: The mechanism of pathogenicity is known to be loss of function.

evidence.reference_title: CLDN16 genotype predicts renal decline in familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.
evidence.snippet: The 23 patients who had mutations resulting in complete loss of function of both alleles were significantly younger at the onset of symptoms than the 46 patients who had at least one mutant allele providing partial function (2.2 versus 5.6 years; P < 0.01).

nodes.description: Progressive loss of GFR beginning in childhood; GFR was already below 60 ml/min per 1.73 m2 at diagnosis in 11 of 33 patients in one series. The rate depends on genotype, with faster decline when neither allele keeps claudin-16 function.

evidence.reference_title: Novel paracellin-1 mutations in 25 families with familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.
evidence.snippet: At the time of diagnosis, the GFR was already decreased to <60 ml/min per 1.73 m(2) for 11 patients.

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective cohort study of familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis due to CLDN16 mutations.
evidence.snippet: During follow-up, renal function declined in 60% of patients; 12% of patients reached CKD stage 3 or 4 and one patient developed end-stage renal failure.

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective cohort study of familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis due to CLDN16 mutations.
evidence.snippet: All cases showed nephrocalcinosis, increased urinary fractional excretion of magnesium and hypercalciuria.

nodes.description: Raised parathyroid hormone before the onset of chronic renal failure, in 76% of the Polish cohort.

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective cohort study of familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis due to CLDN16 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Other disease features included hypomagnesaemia (76%), hyperparathyroidism (76%), hyperuricaemia (56%) and hypocitraturia (60%).

evidence.reference_title: Familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis: clinical and molecular characteristics.
evidence.snippet: Other biochemical anomalies consist of elevated serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels before the onset of chronic renal failure, incomplete distal tubular acidosis, hyperuricaemia and hypocitraturia

nodes.description: Low serum magnesium from renal wasting. It is not universal: 76% in the Polish cohort, and serum magnesium can normalize as GFR falls because less magnesium is filtered.

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective cohort study of familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis due to CLDN16 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Other disease features included hypomagnesaemia (76%), hyperparathyroidism (76%), hyperuricaemia (56%) and hypocitraturia (60%).

evidence.reference_title: Familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis: clinical and molecular characteristics.
evidence.snippet: Hypomagnesaemia may disappear with the deterioration of the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) due to a decline in filtered magnesium.

nodes.description: Paracellular reabsorption of magnesium and calcium in the thick ascending limb fails, so both cations are lost in the urine. Fractional magnesium excretion is high even when serum magnesium is still normal.

evidence.snippet: The primary defect is related to impaired tubular reabsorption of magnesium and calcium in the thick ascending limb of Henle's loop.

evidence.snippet: Renal magnesium ion (Mg2+) resorption occurs predominantly through a paracellular conductance in the thick ascending limb of Henle (TAL).

nodes.description: The only definitive treatment for end-stage disease. Calcium and magnesium excretion normalize after transplantation and the disease does not recur in the graft, which shows the defect is intrinsic to the kidney.

evidence.reference_title: Familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis: clinical and molecular characteristics.
evidence.snippet: Calcium and magnesium excretion is normalized after transplantation and there is no recurrence of the disease.

nodes.description: In the TAL, magnesium and calcium are reabsorbed between cells, driven by a lumen-positive voltage. Claudin-16 behaves as a non-selective cation channel rather than a dedicated magnesium channel, and its interaction with claudin-19 gives the tight junction its cation selectivity. Without it the junction loses cation selectivity, so the driving force and pathway for divalent cation reabsorption are lost.
nodes.id: Loss of Cation-Selective TAL Tight Junction Pathway

animal_models.description: Knockdown mice lose TAL paracellular cation selectivity and develop renal magnesium and calcium wasting with nephrocalcinosis.

evidence.snippet: PCLN-1 is located in tight junctions of the TAL and is related to the claudin family of tight junction proteins.

evidence.reference_title: Claudin-16 and claudin-19 interact and form a cation-selective tight junction complex.
evidence.snippet: Here we showed that in pig kidney epithelial cells, CLDN19 functioned as a Cl(-) blocker, whereas CLDN16 functioned as a Na(+) channel.

evidence.reference_title: Claudin-16 and claudin-19 interact and form a cation-selective tight junction complex.
evidence.snippet: Coexpression of CLDN16 and CLDN19 generated cation selectivity of the TJ in a synergistic manner, and CLDN16 and CLDN19 were observed to interact using several criteria.

evidence.reference_title: Transgenic RNAi depletion of claudin-16 and the renal handling of magnesium.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that claudin-16 plays a key role in maintaining the paracellular cation selectivity of the thick ascending limbs of the nephron.

locations: thick ascending limb of loop of Henle

nodes.description: Oral magnesium salts are given for the hypomagnesemia but have not been shown to change serum magnesium substantially or to slow loss of kidney function.

evidence.reference_title: Familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis: clinical and molecular characteristics.
evidence.snippet: FHHNC patients are given oral magnesium supplementation and thiazide diuretics to prevent the progression of nephrocalcinosis or nephrolithiasis, but neither treatment has had a considerable effect on the levels of urinary calcium or serum magnesium or on the deterioration of renal function

evidence.reference_title: Novel paracellin-1 mutations in 25 families with familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.
evidence.snippet: Treatment with magnesium salts and thiazides seemed to have no effect on the progression of the disease.

nodes.description: Bilateral nephrocalcinosis, present in every patient of the Polish cohort.

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective cohort study of familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis due to CLDN16 mutations.
evidence.snippet: All cases showed nephrocalcinosis, increased urinary fractional excretion of magnesium and hypercalciuria.

evidence.reference_title: Familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis: clinical and molecular characteristics.
evidence.snippet: Patients develop hypomagnesaemia, hypercalciuria and bilateral nephrocalcinosis and their clinical course is often complicated by the development of chronic renal failure.

evidence.reference_title: Familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis: clinical and molecular characteristics.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, patients usually present with recurrent urinary tract infections, nephrolithiasis, polyuria, polydipsia and/or failure to thrive

nodes.description: Chronic kidney disease in FHHNC is accompanied by progressive tubulointerstitial nephritis. Its cause is uncertain: it has been attributed to hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis, but a correlation has not been shown, and a role of claudin-16 in tight junction integrity has been proposed instead.

evidence.reference_title: Familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis: clinical and molecular characteristics.
evidence.snippet: As mentioned before, FHHNC patients usually develop chronic renal failure, which is correlated with progressive tubulointerstitial nephritis; however, its pathophysiology is uncertain.

nodes.description: Inappropriately high fractional magnesium excretion. It was present in every patient of the Polish cohort and is diagnostic even when serum magnesium is normal.

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective cohort study of familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis due to CLDN16 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, we found that normomagnesaemia does not exclude FHHNC and the calculation of fractional excretion of Mg can be diagnostic in the setting of normomagnesaemia.

nodes.description: End-stage renal disease, reached at a median age of 14.5 years by 12 of 33 patients in one series. By age 15, 54% of patients with two complete loss-of-function alleles and 20% of those with residual function need renal replacement therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Novel paracellin-1 mutations in 25 families with familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.
evidence.snippet: Twelve patients exhibited progression to end-stage renal disease, at a median age of 14.5 yr.

nodes.description: Thiazides are used to lower urinary calcium. Reported effects differ: the Polish cohort found that they reduced hypercalciuria in most patients, while earlier series and the 2016 review report no considerable effect on urinary calcium or on progression.

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective cohort study of familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis due to CLDN16 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Treatment with thiazides effectively reduced hypercalciuria in most cases.

evidence.reference_title: Familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis: clinical and molecular characteristics.
evidence.snippet: FHHNC patients are given oral magnesium supplementation and thiazide diuretics to prevent the progression of nephrocalcinosis or nephrolithiasis, but neither treatment has had a considerable effect on the levels of urinary calcium or serum magnesium or on the deterioration of renal function

nodes.description: Founder variant in the first extracellular loop, the most frequent allele in patients from Germany, Poland and eastern Europe.

evidence.reference_title: Novel paracellin-1 mutations in 25 families with familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.
evidence.snippet: The accumulation of mutations affecting the first extracellular loop was striking, with 48% of all mutant alleles exhibiting a Leu151Phe exchange.

evidence.reference_title: Retrospective cohort study of familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis due to CLDN16 mutations.
evidence.snippet: The founder mutation in CLDN16, Leu151Phe, was the most frequent cause of FHHNC in Polish patients, with 13 (52%) cases being homozygous and 5 (20%) carrying Leu151Phe allele in compound heterozygosity.
